source.authors: Griffing AH, Bauer AM, Wegerski AE, Gamble T, Rasys AM
source.title: Embryology reveals a morphological signature of ancestral diurnality maintained in a nocturnal lineage

value: fovea present (described as a foveated gecko)
method: foveated status stated by the paper, which photographed S. macrolepis embryos for eye shape only; no fovea data of its own for this species
where: Results, sentence beginning "To compare these patterns of eye development, we examined stage 33, 37, and 41 specimens"; read in pieces, the quote is the second piece, split before ", and two non-foveated geckos"
quote: two foveated geckos (Phelsuma laticauda and Sphaerodactylus macrolepis; Figure 2D–I)
note: Secondary: the paper names S. macrolepis foveated with no citation at that point; its Introduction says foveae "have been identified in all diurnal sphaerodactylid taxa thus far investigated" (Guerra-Fuentes et al. 2014; Röll 2001b; Underwood 1954), which does not name the species. Primaries not opened.

source.authors: Schleich CE, Vielma A, Glösmann M, Palacios AG, Peichl L
source.title: Retinal photoreceptors of two subterranean tuco-tuco species (Rodentia, Ctenomys): Morphology, topography, and spectral sensitivity

method: photopic spectral electroretinogram fitted by a sum of three visual pigment templates
quote: Unexpectedly, their sensitivity profiles were best fitted by the linear summation of three visual pigment templates with λmax at 370 nm (S pigment, UV), at 510 nm (L pigment), and at 450 nm (an as‐yet unexplained mechanism).
note: Abstract only. The abstract says "Photopic spectral electroretinograms were recorded." and does not name the species they came from; the sentence before speaks of both species (S opsin tuning residues). Logged for both species of the study as the abstract reads; the species of the ERG is not confirmed. DOI as printed in the CONICET record (dc.relation.alternativeid).

source.authors: Lamond AER, Potier S, Fontaine L, Martin GR, Portugal SJ
source.title: The visual impediment of cranial ornamentation in male Chrysolophus pheasants

where: Results, maximum binocular width; the fetch tool returned the sentence in two pieces, 'Maximum binocular width did not differ significantly between the sexes, when both species were combined' and then the quoted piece
note: Pooled over Chrysolophus pictus and C. amherstiae, so it is a genus value and not a value for either species alone. The paper also gives vertical binocular extent (75 degrees in male golden pheasants, 105 in females; 70 and 110 in Lady Amherst's) and a blind sector behind the head (female 49.7, male 60.5 degrees), neither logged as a trait here. Grade g: genus value pooled over two species.

source.authors: Mascaro LDB, Schorn NJ, Souza JM, Ventura DSF (as in the repository page's generated citation, which may be alphabetical)
source.title: Spectral input systems of brazilian bees
source.journal: Reunião Anual da Fesbe, Caxambu (conference abstract)

where: abstract; pieces 15, 16 and 17 of the page text are consecutive; Paratrigona sumuda is named two pieces earlier in the species list (piece 13)
quote: Frieseomelitta, Lestrimellita limão, Partamona subnuda e Schwarziana quadripuntacta). The results confirm the existence of three receptors in all species, with λ max at the UV. (340±8 nm), blue (449±17) and green (524±7); the red receptor was not found.
note: Conference abstract; the species is printed "Paratrigona sumuda", a likely misprint (perhaps for Paratrigona subnuda; the list also has "Partamona subnuda"). The statement is for all 12 species together. Grade g: genus-level record from one ambiguously named member.
